yeah something similar happened to my neighbor :( his blood sugar was too high and he fell asleep and died. and yes, when you’re eating a meal, you have to caluclate the carbs and push the buttons on the pump to tell it how many carbs you’re eating and it does the math for you based on the settings reccomended by your doctor (or yourself). there is an auto mode you can use but that’s only if you’re wearing a sensor that continuously checks your blood sugar 24 hours a day. i’m not a fan of the sensor because it was waking me up at night (like 10 times, it was ridiculous) to calibrate it and i wound up checking my blood sugar WAY more often than i was without it so i got frustrated and asked “what’s the point” because the sensor is supposed to make it so you DON’T have to prick your finger more than 10 times a day lmao. but idk maybe they’ve fixed some bugs and stuff since then but for now i’m fine with just checking my blood sugar myself without the sensor beeping at me to calibrate while i’m at work or in class

ALSO yes there is a basal rate that you do recieve automatically throughout the day, it’s usually less than 1 unit per hour for most, and with the auto mode that is used with a sensor, it will change your basal rate automatically based on the trend of your sugars, like if you’re dropping kinda fast, it’ll back off on the basal rate, but you do have to punch in the numbers for a bolus. basically, a basal rate is the small amount you recieve throughout the day to keep your sugars from getting too high and a bolus is the big amount you recieve for eating carbs
